PullRequest.Title: show migrate customization hint in chat view
PullRequest.Body:

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Direct call-flow evidence proves the new request-path scan and the later invokeAgent ordering; only the filesystem-dependent duration is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem enumeration and customization-list CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold work fans out across three customization types and their configured user/workspace locations; Always runs the computation each request and Once retries until a hint is found.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased request latency on the chat critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Sending a chat request did not compute migration candidates or await customization discovery.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Chat sends now perform migration discovery and await its result before invoking the selected agent.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1580 newly calls computeMigrationHint from every eligible request; this work was absent from the base send path.
Findings.Title: Move migration discovery off the send critical path
Findings.Impact: With the experiment set to Once or Always, the first agent-host request after startup or prompt-cache invalidation waits for customization filesystem discovery, delaying agent startup and first response in slow or multi-root workspaces.
Findings.Evidence: computeMigrationHint calls computeMigrations, which lists agent, instruction, and prompt files. On a cold or invalidated cache, listPromptFiles traverses configured user/workspace locations through PromptFilesLocator. The enclosing Promise.all is awaited at line 1655-1658, while invokeAgent is not reached until line 1840.
Findings.Recommendation: Populate an event-invalidated hint cache outside request dispatch, or emit the hint asynchronously without awaiting it before invokeAgent, and use the request cancellation token.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send an agent-host chat request with migration hints set to Once or Always
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request creates its UI model, then awaits hooks, instructions, and the new migration hint together. Migration discovery must finish before participant activation, MCP autostart, and chatAgentService.invokeAgent, so it directly delays agent dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover agent, instruction, and prompt files across configured user and workspace locations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three logical prompt-type listings per hint computation. On a cold/invalidated cache, each type fans out to user and local discovery and then across its configured locations; warm successful lists are shared per type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The chat send path did not enumerate migration candidates; these filesystem listings were not required to dispatch the agent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All cold discovery completes before invokeAgent can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate extension prompt-file providers and request their files for agent, instructions, and prompt types.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to three activation events plus one provider call per registered provider of each type on a cold/invalidated list; cached list promises avoid this on warm reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Migration-related extension provider enumeration was not on the chat request path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider activation/listing is transitively awaited by migration discovery before agent dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured customization source folders, workspace roots, registered extension providers, and files in the three queried customization types. Always recomputes each request; Once also retries each request when no migration hint is found.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: computeMigrations runs UserData and PromptFiles in parallel; UserData lists agent and instructions in parallel, yielding three concurrent list operations. Each list also fans out user/local/extension discovery. Source-folder queries are sequential per migration branch, with the two branches concurrent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PromptsService caches successful per-type file lists and invalidates them on file/provider/configuration events, coalescing concurrent cold calls. There is no cache for the derived migration hint or negative result, so warm requests still filter complete lists and query candidate target folders; no-candidate Once requests repeat indefinitely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added awaited call, transitive filesystem/provider implementations, cache behavior, and later invokeAgent ordering are explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The setting defaults to Never, but its experiment mode can enable Once or Always. Exact delay depends on provider activation and filesystem/workspace latency; cold remote or multi-root workspaces have the highest cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity latency regression because display-only migration discovery is newly placed on the agent-dispatch critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send chat when hints are Never, workspace-dismissed, already shown in Once mode, or the session is not an agent-host target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: collectCustomizationMigrationHint performs configuration/state/storage checks and returns before calling the migration service; existing hook/instruction collection remains the dispatch prerequisite.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One request and one session-state/storage-key lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new expensive task is added to the Promise.all after the synchronous guard returns.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The dismissal and Once-shown states act as effective negative guards; no migration discovery cache is consulted or needed on these paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the explicit short-circuit conditions and tests covering Never, dismissal, local, and extension-host sessions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance; configuration and in-memory state reads are bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression on guarded paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismiss migration hints from the notification
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user click resolves the active session type and writes one workspace-scoped storage value; it is not on chat dispatch or rendering critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist one workspace-scoped boolean dismissal key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per explicit dismissal action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration-hint dismissal key was written because the feature did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the click action waits synchronously for store invocation; future requests avoid migration discovery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per user click and one key per session type.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single user-triggered write with no loop or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persisted positive dismissal is read on later requests and suppresses all hint work; keys are naturally bounded by the small set of harness session types used in a workspace.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage implementation may flush asynchronously, but cardinality is constant.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance issue; bounded persistence prevents future request-path work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Register the migration-hint configuration and render an emitted hint
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration schema registration occurs during contribution setup. Markdown/link allocation and one progress callback happen only after discovery returns a message; they are minor compared with discovery and do not cross subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One schema entry at startup and one small MarkdownString per emitted hint; Always can emit one per request by design.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed for the small static schema or link strings; the expensive derived hint itself is not cached, which is covered by the reported request scenario.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from changed configuration and notification construction code.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all nine changed files. One medium-severity critical-path latency finding was submitted: enabled migration hints await cold filesystem/extension discovery before agent invocation. Dismissal, guarded requests, configuration registration, and notification rendering are bounded and add no separate performance issue.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
